diagram_math_checks.objects_and_conventions: V=k^{n+1}; P(V) uses lines, consistent with the Plucker supplier which sends a subspace to the line spanned by its wedge. The dual point [a] is the line ka in V*, not a quotient of V*. Equivalently a nonzero a gives the one-dimensional quotient V -> V/ker(a), up to a choice of coordinate in that quotient. The hyperplane is P(ker a).

diagram_math_checks.relation: I consists exactly of ([x],[a]) with a(x)=sum a_i x_i=0. Independent rescaling of x and a multiplies the value by a nonzero product and preserves its vanishing.

diagram_math_checks.maps: p:I -> P^n sends ([x],[a]) to [x]; q:I -> (P^n)^vee sends ([x],[a]) to [a]. Each is the restriction of the indicated product projection. Both arrows point from I to their stated codomains; there is no map or commutativity claim between the bases.
diagram_math_checks.local_basis: Original Example ambient product and fixed-[a]/fixed-[x] fibre statements; incidence supplier explicitly supplies two projections.

diagram_math_checks.fibres_and_dimensions: For fixed nonzero x, evaluation V* -> k is a surjective linear functional, so p^{-1}([x]) is P(ann(x)) with ann(x) of dimension n. For fixed nonzero a, a:V -> k is surjective, so q^{-1}([a]) is P(ker a) with kernel dimension n. Thus for every base point when n>=1 both fibres are P^{n-1}; the diagram does not weaken this to a generic-fibre assertion or assert a canonical identification.

diagram_math_checks.boundary_cases: For n=1 each n-dimensional kernel is a line and its projectivization is a single point. For n=0 both ambient vector spaces have dimension one, evaluation/nonzero a have zero kernels, and no pair of nonzero representatives has a(x)=0; I and both fibres are empty. Diagram explicitly restricts P^{n-1} labels to n>=1 and never uses P^{-1}.
